clue.text: Underlying principle, one accepted by male singer

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken in by it, so the singer's letters go around the one

parts.note: a bass is a male singer with the lowest voice
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A reasoned point of principle is taken on board by a deep-voiced singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the foundation on which an idea rests, a synonym for an underlying principle.

clue.text: Lieutenant initially entering HQ in Swiss city

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it, so the initial letter sits within the headquarters word

parts.note: a base is a headquarters

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word Lieutenant

explanation.surface: An army lieutenant arrives first at headquarters set in a Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: BASLE is the traditional English spelling of Basel, on the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Basle is a city in northern Switzerland, so this is a straightforward example of the category.

clue.text: Cutting energetic exercise

definitions.meaning: missing or leaving out, as when someone misses a class
jumping over a rope again and again, a vigorous workout

explanation.surface: A demanding workout that slims the body down.
explanation.definitionFit: Skipping both means omitting something and names the rope-jumping exercise.

clue.text: Indian instrument, one held by celebrity

indicators.note: something held by another is enclosed within it, so the one goes inside the celebrity word

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A famous musician clutches a single Indian instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked plucked lute from the Indian classical tradition.

clue.text: Choosing the best job in fruit farm?

definitions.meaning: selecting only the most attractive options for oneself
literally the task of harvesting small red stone fruit from trees; the question mark flags the literal reading

explanation.surface: A worker on an orchard gets to select the most desirable task.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means taking only the most favourable items, drawn from harvesting the ripest fruit.

clue.text: Abstruse remedy introduced by old surgeon

indicators.note: a thing introduced by others has them coming before it, so the remedy word goes last

parts.note: BS is Bachelor of Surgery, a surgeon's qualification
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: A former surgeon presents a little-understood treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: BS stands for Bachelor of Surgery, the degree held by a surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstruse and obscure are synonyms, both describing ideas hard to understand.

clue.text: Way English teacher originally let it remain

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word teacher

explanation.surface: An English teacher marking work tells a pupil to leave a passage alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is the Latin proofreading mark instructing that a deleted passage should stand.

clue.text: Obsequiously flatter a mostly dreary goddess

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word but not its last letter

parts.note: dull means dreary
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A worshipper fawns over a somewhat tedious deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims DULL to DUL. Ate is a Greek goddess, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate is to praise someone excessively and servilely, which is fawning flattery.

clue.text: Dressed like monk, fellow lived in

parts.note: a monk wears a habit, so dressed like one is in a habit
Ed is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A man clad in a monk's robe made his home somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A house that is inhabited is one people have occupied, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Go round in woman's garment

definitions.meaning: to pass around the edge of something rather than through it
a piece of clothing hanging from the waist, worn by women

explanation.surface: Someone walks about wearing a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirt as a verb means to circle the edge; as a noun it is the garment.

clue.text: Article cracking up musical performance

indicators.note: cracking up suggests breaking apart, so the letters of Article are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece falls to pieces just like a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a concert given by a soloist or small group, a kind of musical performance.

clue.text: Traveller in capital backing sovereign

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the whole combination is read in reverse
in puts the traveller inside the capital

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
a rep, a commercial traveller, is a travelling salesman

explanation.surface: A tourist in the capital supports the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the whole combination ROREPME; a rep is a sales representative who travels for work.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme monarch, so a sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Richard III, say — king one encountered in strange story

indicators.note: something encountered in another is found inside it, so the two letters go within the rearranged word
strange means unusual, signalling the letters of story are rearranged

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Richard III is a king met in an odd tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges STORY into YORST, and K and I go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard III was the last king of the House of York, one member of that dynasty.

clue.text: Show tabby, possibly, kept by private record company

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it, so the animal goes within the record label word

parts.note: an indie is an independent, privately owned record label
a tabby is an example of a cat

explanation.surface: A small record label looks after a striped pet in its office.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to point out or make plain, a synonym of the verb show.

clue.text: Smokers' requisite lost outside entrance to hotel

indicators.note: outside means the first word wraps around the next letter

parts.note: astray means lost or gone off course

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Smoking items have gone missing outside a hotel doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashtray is a dish for cigarette ash, a standard accessory for anyone who smokes.

clue.text: Fellow protégés, lily-livered types

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning fellow, as in co-worker
wards are young people placed under a guardian's protection

explanation.surface: Fellow pupils of a mentor are faint-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily-livered is an old term for timid or spineless, so lily-livered types are those lacking courage.

clue.text: Italian gentlemen so ignore it endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means each of the three words loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to disregard some Italian men forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the end of each word: SO, IGNORE and IT lose O, E and T, leaving S, IGNOR and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Signori is the Italian plural of signor, the courtesy title for men, so Italian gentlemen.

clue.text: Crimson vehicle belonging to the present compiler

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
the setter speaking of himself would say the thing is his own, so it is mine

explanation.surface: The setter drives a deep red car.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a deep vivid red pigment, a near synonym for crimson.

clue.text: Argument over extremely disorderly hooligan

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or argument

indicators.note: extremely means taking the letters at the extremes, first and last, of disorderly

explanation.surface: A quarrel about a thoroughly unruly lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy is a noisy, rough person, an informal noun close to hooligan.

clue.text: Press chief engages male staff to edit

indicators.note: to engage staff is to take them on, so the men are taken inside the editor's letters

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper
men are male staff members

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor hires men to revise copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and improve it, a synonym for editing it.

clue.text: Change direction on can — it provides security

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the sailing word follows the container word

parts.note: a tin is a can
to tack is to change course when sailing

explanation.surface: A yachtsman turns about while sitting on a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin-tack is a small nail that holds things firmly in place, so it fastens and secures.

clue.text: Well-turned-out ox, for example

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for a bovine animal, of which an ox is one

explanation.surface: An unexpectedly smart-looking bullock.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means tidy in appearance, and is also an old word for cattle, as in neatsfoot oil.

clue.text: Sea creature's plaintive cry you can hear

indicators.note: you can hear points to a word sounding like another

parts.note: a wail is a mournful, plaintive cry

explanation.surface: A sea creature's mournful song is audible.
explanation.definitionFit: The whale is a large marine mammal, a classic sea creature.

clue.text: Resigned from music group, one featuring in commercial

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing inside, so the group and one go within the commercial

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a band is a music group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician has quit a band after appearing in a television advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Resigned can mean given up for lost; abandoned shares that sense of having relinquished something.

clue.text: Give up and give in

definitions.meaning: to surrender or submit to pressure

explanation.surface: Two near-identical phrases for surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: Yield means both to produce or hand over something and to concede defeat.
